citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A white male poodle "Jasper" has not had appropriate treatments to address his dental disease. During the inspection,
Jasper had moderate amounts of hardened brown material adhered to most of the upper teeth. The gums have receded
from the surface of the tooth on several upper premolars and canines. Additionally, there is a white to yellow material
where the gums meet the teeth of the upper premolars. The left upper first premolar was loose and the second premolar
appeared to be missing. The veterinarian had examined this dog in November 2025 and instructed that the dog needed to
have a dental cleaning within the next 6 months (by May 2026). At the time of the inspection, this dog's dental disease
had not been treated.
Dental disease can not only cause pain and infection in the mouth, but also may lead to infection elsewhere in the body,
such as liver or heart. It is important to promptly treat disease in accordance with the veterinarian's instructions.
Correct by using appropriate methods to treat this dog's dental disease and to diagnose, prevent, control, and treat other
diseases and injuries in all dogs.
Correct by 9/30/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
